name: job-queue
description: A background job queue service from written requirements: priorities, a worker pool, retries with exponential backoff, dead jobs, pause and resume, persistence across a restart (running jobs return to the queue). Judged by hidden HTTP checks that time the workers.

input.request: A background job queue HTTP service. POST /jobs with JSON {type, payload?, priority?, maxAttempts?} queues a job and answers 201 with the job. type is one of "echo" (succeeds; its result is the payload), "fail" (always fails with the error "failed on purpose") or "flaky" (fails while its attempts so far are fewer than payload.failTimes, then succeeds with the payload as result). payload is an optional JSON object; payload.ms (default 0) is how long every attempt of that job takes, in milliseconds, before it succeeds or fails. priority is an integer 0-9 (default 5): higher runs first, and jobs of equal priority run in the order they were queued. maxAttempts is an integer 1-10 (default 3). Anything else is 400 with a JSON error; malformed JSON is 400; a body over 10 KB is 413. A pool of WORKERS (environment variable, default 2) runs jobs concurrently, never more at once. A failed attempt with attempts left puts the job back in the queue, not to run before BACKOFF_MS * 2^(attempts - 1) milliseconds after the failure (BACKOFF_MS environment variable, default 1000); with no attempts left the job is "dead" and keeps its last error. A job is {id, type, payload, priority, maxAttempts, status, attempts, result, error, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt}: status is queued, running, succeeded or dead; attempts counts attempts started; startedAt is when its latest attempt started and finishedAt when it succeeded or died (both null until then; timestamps in milliseconds since the epoch). GET /jobs/:id returns a job (404 with a JSON error for an unknown id). GET /jobs lists all jobs newest first; GET /jobs?status=dead (any status) only those, and an unknown status is 400. POST /jobs/:id/retry puts a dead job back in the queue with attempts 0 (200 with the job); any other status is 409. DELETE /jobs/:id removes a queued or dead job (204); a running one is 409. GET /stats answers {queued, running, succeeded, dead}. POST /workers/pause stops workers from taking new jobs (running ones finish) and POST /workers/resume starts them again, both 200; the service starts unpaused. Jobs survive a restart: the state is in the file DATA_FILE (environment variable), written atomically, and a job that was running when the service stopped is queued again when it starts (its attempt is not counted). The port comes from PORT.
input.stack: Node.js 22, no external dependencies (node:http, node:test), persistence in a JSON file written atomically. npm start runs the service.
